stem:
Boman has a pile of identical beads and an ordered clap sequence: first clap, second clap, third clap, and so on. He wants the clap sequence to represent how many beads are in the pile.

Which claim correctly states what he must do?

options.text: Match each bead to exactly one clap in order, with no bead left unmatched and no clap left unused for a bead.
Clap once for the whole pile, then name the size from the sound alone.
Match some beads to two claps so the sequence runs longer than the pile.
Skip matching the last few beads once the claps sound familiar.

teacher.key_rationale: Counting needs a one-to-one match between beads and an ordered standard sequence. One clap for the pile, double-matching, or skipping beads break that mapping.
